fullDescription:
Three and a half hours on the limestone that made Railay one of the best-known climbing destinations in the world.

Railay's rock is the reason climbers fly here specifically. Tropical limestone weathers into pockets, tufas and stalactites, which means the holds are features you grab rather than edges you pinch, and the walls overhang in a way that looks impossible from the beach and turns out to be climbable. Routes run from beginner slabs to some of the hardest sport climbs in Asia, often on the same crag.

Beginners are the default here rather than an afterthought. The instructor sets up top ropes, so the rope runs from an anchor above you and you are held the moment you let go. Nothing on the first day needs upper-body strength: climbing is legs, and most of a first session is the instructor getting people to stop hauling with their arms and start standing up on their feet.

Multiple routes are set so you move on when you have done one rather than repeating it, and the instruction adapts if you have climbed before.

The setting is the other half. The crags sit above the beach with the Andaman behind you, so you are looking out over water the whole way up.

All climbing gear, harness, shoes and safety equipment is provided. Railay has no road access, so the trip includes the boat crossing as part of getting there.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers a professional climbing instructor, safety equipment, climbing gear, multiple routes and personalised instruction for those with experience.

Wear something you can move in. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: The limestone that made Railay a world climbing destination
Pockets, tufas and stalactites rather than flat edges
Top rope, so you are held the moment you let go
Climbing is legs: no upper-body strength needed
All gear provided, routes set for your level

fullDescription:
A full day out to the Similans, which are a different sea from anything closer to Krabi.

The Similans are nine granite islands out in the Andaman, and the granite is the point. Everything else you snorkel on this coast is limestone; here the rock weathers into huge rounded boulders above and below the waterline, so the underwater landscape is boulder fields and swim-throughs rather than coral shelf. Visibility is routinely the best in Thailand, which is why divers plan trips around these islands specifically.

Because the islands sit far offshore and inside a national park, the water is clear of river outflow and the fish life is noticeably denser than on the coastal reefs.

The one thing to plan around: **the Similans close every year**, roughly from mid-October or November through to April or May, under national park rules that let the reef recover through the monsoon. The exact dates are set by the park authority and shift year to year, so confirm before you build a trip around it.

Breakfast and an international buffet lunch are included, and hotel pickup covers Krabi downtown, Klong Muang Beach and Ao Nang Beach if you select that option.

Nine hours with a long transfer at each end makes this the biggest day on the Krabi list. It is a speedboat across open sea, so anyone who feels the water should take something before boarding rather than after.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final.

National park fees are collected separately unless confirmed otherwise. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Granite islands: boulder fields, not coral shelf
Among the clearest water anywhere in Thailand
Far offshore, so denser fish life than coastal reefs
Closed by the national park roughly November to April
Breakfast, buffet lunch and Krabi-area pickup included

fullDescription:
Seven islands across an afternoon and evening on a longtail fitted out for the length of the day.

Eight hours on a standard longtail is a long time on a hard bench. The premium version is the same boat type with the seating, shade and space sorted out, which on this trip is most of what you are paying for.

The afternoon start inverts the usual Krabi day. Morning boats all reach the same beaches inside the same hour; leaving later means arriving at the final stops as the fleet turns for home, so the last islands of this trip are quieter than the same islands were at midday.

Snorkelling happens while there is light, over shallow reef the guide picks on the day according to tide and water clarity. Sunset is taken from the water, and Krabi's limestone holds colour long after the sun has gone.

The guide works in English and Thai. That matters more than it sounds on a boat: the crew are local, and the person who can talk to both them and you is the one who can change the plan when the sea does.

Check one thing when booking: hotel transfers are marked as depending on the option selected. Confirm yours includes them, or work out how you are reaching the pier.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the English and Thai-speaking guide, the boat, snorkelling mask and life jacket, with round-trip hotel transfers if your option includes them.

Eight hours. National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Longtail fitted out for an eight-hour day
Afternoon start: last stops after the fleet leaves
Snorkel stops chosen on the day for tide and clarity
Guide works in Thai as well as English
Check whether transfers are in your chosen option

fullDescription:
A six-hour island run with two proper snorkelling stops and Phra Nang Cave Beach, on a traditional longtail with a local crew.

Two snorkelling stops rather than one is the difference here. Most Krabi island trips fit snorkelling around the beach time; this one treats it as half the day. Krabi's reef sits shallow and close to the islands, so you do not need to be a strong swimmer or go out of your depth, and in several places you can stand.

Phra Nang Cave Beach is on the Railay peninsula, which has no road access at all, so it can only be reached by boat. The beach sits under an overhanging limestone cliff, and at one end is the shrine where fishermen leave carved wooden offerings to a spirit they believe protects them at sea. It is still in use rather than preserved for visitors.

The crew are experienced local boatmen rather than a tour company's rotating staff. On this coast that shows in where they anchor and which stop they pick when the wind turns.

Pickup covers Ao Nang and Klong Muang, which is worth noting if you are staying outside the main strip: a lot of Krabi boat trips only collect from Ao Nang.

Six hours is a comfortable length. Long enough to swim properly at both snorkel stops and at the beaches, short enough to leave your evening free.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off from Ao Nang and Klong Muang, the traditional longtail, an experienced local crew and a local guide.

National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Two full snorkelling stops, not one fitted around the beaches
Shallow enough to stand in at several spots
Phra Nang beach, reachable only by boat
Experienced local crew who read the wind
Pickup from Klong Muang as well as Ao Nang

fullDescription:
The four islands by speedboat, which buys you time at each stop rather than time on the water.

A longtail takes most of the day to work the same circuit. A speedboat covers the distance between islands in a fraction of it, and the hours saved go into being on the beaches instead of travelling to them. Six hours on a speedboat covers what a longtail needs eight or nine to do.

The route is Poda, Chicken Island, Tup and Mor. Thale Waek, the Separated Sea, is the sandbar that surfaces as the tide drops and links the islands into a walkable strip, then disappears as the water returns. Whether you walk it depends on the tide that day, not the operator.

Snorkelling is over shallow coral close to the beaches. Krabi's reef is forgiving: you do not need to swim out or go deep to see it, and several stops are shallow enough to stand in.

A buffet lunch is included, along with seasonal fruit through the day.

One honest note on speedboats: they are fast and they pound. On flat water it is nothing; in any chop the ride is hard on backs and on anyone prone to seasickness. Take something before boarding rather than after if that is a concern.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off, a professional guide, buffet lunch, snorkelling equipment and seasonal fruit.

Six hours. National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Speedboat, so more time on beaches and less in transit
Poda, Chicken Island, Tup and Mor in six hours
Walk the Thale Waek sandbar when the tide drops
Shallow snorkelling, standable at several stops
Buffet lunch and fruit through the day

fullDescription:
A guided run through Ao Nang's bars over five hours, which solves the problem of arriving somewhere alone and not knowing where anything is.

Ao Nang's nightlife is spread along the beach road and up the side sois, and the difference between the bars is not obvious from outside. A crawl fixes that in the way a map cannot: you walk in with a group that is already talking to each other, and the guide knows which places are worth the stop on that night of the week.

The wristband is the part that keeps working after the group breaks up. It carries discounts at the venues on the route, so the rest of your stay in Ao Nang is cheaper than it would have been.

The vest marks the group, which sounds silly and is the reason strangers talk to you. For solo travellers, that is the whole product.

Practical things worth knowing. Ao Nang is compact and the whole route is walkable, so nobody needs transport. Thai bar measures are generous rather than metered, and buckets are shared drinks built for a group rather than a single serving, so pace yourself against the five-hour length rather than the first hour. Keep your phone and cash in a front pocket; the beach road gets crowded late.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the pub crawl vest, a bucket, pour shots along the route, and the discount wristband.

Five hours, starting at KOKO Hostel. Bring ID. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Guided route through Ao Nang's bars, all walkable
Wristband keeps giving discounts after the night ends
Vest marks the group, which is why strangers talk to you
Built for solo travellers arriving without a plan
Thai measures are generous: pace against five hours
